legal.summary: What does the law say about a fixed work plan?
legal.intro: Section 4 b of the Danish Working Time Act requires an objective, reliable and accessible system that can measure the daily working time of each employee. According to the preparatory works of the bill and the Ministry of Employment, working time may be recorded in advance according to a fixed work plan, so that only deviations (overtime, shorter days, absence) are recorded when they happen. This is how this page works.
legal.quote1: § 4 b. To ensure compliance with the applicable rules on daily and weekly rest periods and maximum weekly working time, the employer must introduce an objective, reliable and accessible working time registration system that makes it possible to measure the daily working time of each of the employees concerned. (Unofficial translation)
legal.quote2: Subsection 2. The employer must ensure that the employee can access their own data in the working time registration system referred to in subsection 1.
legal.quote3: Subsection 3. The employer must keep the data recorded under subsection 1 for 5 years after the end of the period that forms the basis for calculating the employee's average weekly working time.
legal.point1: The plan can only be changed from today onwards, so earlier days can always be documented as they were.
legal.point2: Every deviation is logged with who and when in the organisation's event log.
legal.point3: You can always download your own records as CSV (subsection 2).
legal.source: Source: the Danish Working Time Act, consolidated act no. 982 of 12 August 2024, § 4 b (retsinformation.dk), checked {date}. This is guidance, not legal advice. Collective agreements may set other requirements.
